source: BBOC 2025 Big 12 Season Preview Part 1+2 (Stuckey/Collin Wilson)

teams.key_avoids: AVOIDS Iowa State + Texas Tech from the top seven. 5 Big 12 home games; road slate is Oklahoma State, Cincinnati, Arizona, TCU — plays none of the projected top 5-6 on the road. But BRUTAL non-con: at Auburn (small dog) then at SMU.
teams.key_injury: Sawyer Robertson leg/head injury history — reported healthy but must stay healthy; offense peaks when he can run.
teams.bboc_notes: Stuckey's pick to win the Big 12 — he has less than a point separating the top four. Offense was top-10 over the final 7 games under Jake Spavital (Y1), ~40 pts/500 yds, and returns a ton including OL and WR (Ashton Hawkins ruled eligible). The whole question is the secondary: 127th in defending pass explosiveness, and Aranda (back calling D) must fix the back end. Collin likes Baylor a lot but has real issues — Sawyer Robertson graded 15-16 big-time-throws-to-turnover-worthy-plays and only 69th on-target, and 9 of 16 mistakes came in clean pockets. Front seven improved via 750+ lbs of Tulane/A&M interior beef plus coverage LBs (Trevion Barnes FIU, Bob White Tulane). Both hosts want to WAIT for a number — hope Auburn beats them up week one so the Big 12 price drops after the Iowa State–Kansas State winner takes pole position. Freshman kicker a concern in close games.

teams.key_avoids: HOSTS the contenders — Texas Tech, Arizona State, Kansas State all come to Rice-Eccles. Faces only ONE top-7 on the road (at Baylor, late, both off byes). Easy non-con (at UCLA, at Wyoming, Cal Poly). Bye weeks land favorably before top-tier games; Kansas State hits them on back-to-back road travel.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts love Utah after a disastrous 5-7, 1-5 in one-score games. They brought in Devon Dampier and his New Mexico OC Jason Beck to install a spread-option, run-heavy (~55%) tempo attack — no more Cam Rising availability mystery. The OL is arguably the best in the country (~6,800 snaps back, two potential first-round tackles, Joe Moore straw-poll favorite). Dampier created a missed tackle on 34% of 160 carries; brings slot weapon Brian Davis (2.1 YPRR). Concerns: WR room thin (lost their top options), and Dampier's passing/health (58% comp, 12 INTs in a big step up from the ACC). Trust Morgan Scalley's 4-2-5 defense (best front six in the Big 12, top-20 havoc). Stuckey projects 7.84/7.9, Collin 8.8. Collin's real bet is Utah +280 to make the Big 12 title game — loves the tiebreaker/home-heavy edge; makes even the road game at Baylor Utah -1.

teams.key_avoids: AVOIDS Baylor, Utah, and Texas Tech. Only 4 Big 12 home games plus neutral vs Kansas State in Dublin (week zero) — but that buys THREE bye weeks in conference play. Road games (Cincinnati, Colorado, Oklahoma State, TCU) have no true road game vs the top 5-6; TCU is the toughest road trip. SOS ~35th.
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT — the sharpest disagreement of Part 1. Reached the Big 12 title game and won a program-record 11 games despite 13 starters missing time; 5-1 in one-score games, +9 turnovers (regression flags). Stuckey is OUT: lost two 1,000-yd WRs to the NFL, lost center + LT to the NFL (remaining OL was bad in 2023), lost four of top six in a secondary that carried the D, and the DL can't get pressure — he projects 7.2 and leans under. Collin is 100% IN and takes them 12-1 to WIN the league: argues they go back to true Matt Campbell 12/13-personnel football with three big TEs (Burkle, Bramer) and short passing that returns Becht to his 2.6% TOWP freshman form. Edge Tomotoa McDonald (Yale) must stabilize the 3-3-5 front; Caleb Bacon back from injury. Whoever wins the week-zero Kansas State game is in the driver's seat.

teams.key_avoids: Plays FIVE of the other top six — only AVOIDS Kansas State. 5 Big 12 home games but a top-tier road slate: at Baylor, at Utah (off a bye), at Iowa State, at Colorado. Structure: easy first three (at Miss State tricky), BRUTAL middle six, on-paper-easy last three. One bye, in the middle.
teams.key_injury: Sam Leavitt must stay healthy — lost the Cincy game last year when he sat. Injury timing is the season swing (middle-six stretch).
teams.bboc_notes: Defending Big 12 champ running it back — ~17 returning starters, #2 in returning production, 6-1 in one-score games with +14 turnovers (heavy regression flags). The core question both hosts fixate on: how much was Cam Skattebo worth? He was 18% of receiving yards and 65% of rushing yards, and the entire Dillingham/Arroyo philosophy abused LBs on dumps/wheels to him. Replacement Kanyon Udo (Army) had TWO career targets — Collin argues the offense fundamentally changes and defenses can now double Jordan Tyson (3.0 YPRR) and Sam Leavitt (13 BTT/5 TOWP). Defense returns nearly everyone (only real loss is NB Simmons); run D strong, pass D shaky, special teams were a disaster (improved via Gomez, Eastern Michigan). Stuckey projects 8.6, no interest at 6-1. Collin projects ~7.5 and is UNDER 8.5 (-105) — four road games too tough; only takes over if he had Udo.

teams.key_avoids: AVOIDS only Arizona State from the top. 4 Big 12 home / 4 away plus a neutral opener vs Iowa State in Dublin (week zero) — buys bye-week structure. Road games Utah, Baylor, Kansas, Oklahoma State. Scary passing attacks (TCU, Baylor, Texas Tech) all bunched mid-season — could cost them a title shot.
teams.key_injury: OL injury questions in camp (media barred from 11-on-11s); five-star TE Linkon Cure dealing with an injury.
teams.bboc_notes: Should have been better — outgained 12 of 13 opponents, went 8-4. Avery Johnson returns but must take a step: better footwork, more consistent passing, and stay healthy (electric when he runs). HOST SPLIT on direction. The OL went from elite to a question — lost three starters incl. both tackles and the OL coach; counting on George Fitzpatrick (Ohio State, couldn't crack the field, medical issue). Collin is OUT on the offense: hates Johnson at ~190 lbs behind a rebuilt line (center Heck 89th, LG Portier 141st PFF) and his 2-BTT/7-TOWP under pressure = freshman numbers. DL likely the best in the conference (Osuna, Sami, Stufflebean), but the secondary lost three to the NFL. Collin's math says 8.9 and he's actually OVER 8.5 but 'uncomfortable'; Stuckey bet 8.57 and passes; no interest in the league future (too juiced).

teams.key_avoids: AVOIDS Baylor, TCU, and Iowa State. Only 4 Big 12 home games — assumed 7-0 at home (Kansas, Okla State, BYU, UCF). FIVE Big 12 road games (Utah, Arizona State, Kansas State, Houston, West Virginia), all potential tiebreakers — the season hinges there. Soft non-con (Pine Bluff, Kent State, Oregon State home) = easiest overall schedule (~70th SOS).
teams.key_injury: Behren Morton had off-season shoulder surgery — must stay healthy (Will Hammond, RS freshman, is the backup); RT injuries (Zam Branno, Scary) may force a freshman RT.
teams.bboc_notes: The hype team — best portal class in the country (21 commits, 13 four-stars; the rest of the Big 12 signed 12 four-stars combined) via the Matador Club money. Both hosts say it 'feels exactly like Ole Miss' and the number is inflated. DL is probably the best in the Big 12 after adding Lee Hunter (UCF), Gill Howard (NIU), David Bailey (Stanford edge); LBs Jacob Rodriguez + Ben Roberts (209 combined tackles). New OC Mac Leftwich (Air Raid) and new DC Shiel Wood (3-4 hybrid) are praised — Collin calls Wood one of the best coordinator hires nobody's discussing. The fade logic is Joey McGuire on the road: 15-5 at home but 6-10 SU on the road, and every hard game is away. Collin makes it exactly 8.0 and is firing UNDER 8.5 (+120); Stuckey is close to 9 but passes — host split on the number, both skeptical of the hype.

teams.key_avoids: AVOIDS Utah and Texas Tech; hosts Baylor and Iowa State. Only 4 Big 12 home games and a TOUGH non-con (at UNC, hosts SMU). Faces four of the top six. Back-to-back road spot (at BYU/Provo then at Houston off a bye); Baylor comes to Fort Worth off a bye. Last year they dodged the top four and drew the bottom seven — not repeated.
teams.bboc_notes: Best recruiter in the Big 12 (top-25 nationally, #1 in-conference three years running) under Sonny Dykes — builds and develops rather than raiding the portal. Josh Hoover returns for his first full off-season with Kendal Briles, but must replace his top THREE WRs (all on NFL rosters) — Eric McAlister (2.9 YPRR, 11.5 aDOT) is the home-run hitter. Hoover's flaw: 127 pressured drop-backs produced ONE big-time throw and eight turnover-worthy plays, so the mid-tier OL (freshman LT Hughes is key) is pivotal. No run game last year; DL must generate havoc (122nd pass rush, 84th havoc) for a secondary that lost both corners to the NFL — Andy Avalos (Y2) is the havoc guy. Collin nitpicks everything but his number says over: he's near 8.1, prefers over 7 (-125) at Circa. Stuckey projects 7.5, leans over 6.5, and is eyeing UNC as a season-opener upset.

teams.key_avoids: AVOIDS Baylor, Arizona State, and TCU — faces the projected bottom four. Back home after the Kansas City opener. Collin's path to 5 conference wins: home vs West Virginia (off the Backyard Brawl), Cincinnati, Oklahoma State; road at UCF and Arizona — all winnable; hosts Utah in the finale for a chaos scenario.
teams.key_injury: Jalon Daniels health is the whole season — wasn't healthy early last year, didn't practice in spring; can vanish from lineups with no warning.
teams.bboc_notes: One of Stuckey's three sleeper nominees (18-1). Should have been better in 2024 — 1-5 in one-score games, led in the 4th in 10 games, then got hot and beat ranked teams. But MASSIVE attrition: 38 seniors gone, 9 players on NFL rosters, 7,000+ pass-catcher snaps lost (Grimm, Arnold, Skinner + RB Neal), plus three OL to the NFL and both All-American corners (Dotson, Bryant). New OC (internal, Jim Zebrowski) reverts to the heavy pre-snap-motion Lubick/Cody-Nickel scheme that fits Daniels — a schematic bump if the timing holds (watch the Fresno opener). New DC (internal) must find pressure; D was 126th in line yards, 117th in contested catches. Collin bet the Big 12 win-total OVER 4.5 (makes them 5.4 conf wins); Stuckey projects ~6.8, close to market. Path to sleeper: Daniels stays healthy, athletic WRs step up, D transfers hit.

teams.key_avoids: AVOIDS Utah, Kansas State, and Iowa State. 5 Big 12 home games. Both hosts flag a potential 4-0 start; the road slate (Oklahoma State, UCF, Baylor, Arizona State) is 'as good as you can ask for' — especially at Oregon State the week AFTER the Civil War (Beavers flat). Second-half tougher (Arizona State, at Baylor).
teams.bboc_notes: Collin's long-shot FAVORITE to win the Big 12 (35-1) — the Willie Fritz year-two program-builder angle (his Y2 history: 9-2 Blinn, 8-3 Central Missouri, 14-1 Sam Houston, 8-4 Georgia Southern). Top-20 in returning production, jumped from ~national-average experience to top-30. Conner Weigman (17 BTT/21 TOWP in three A&M years) is the reclamation bet — 'it can't get worse than last year' (9 TD/17 INT). OC Slade Nagel back next to Fritz for the inside-out, run-first, huge-OL philosophy (avg 6'5"/315; #3 portal class in the Big 12); love TE Tanner Koziol (Ball State). DL added Eddie Valles (FIU, 40 pressures) — Austin Armstrong blitz-heavy, was 126th in pass rush. Concern: the secondary (lost Halsey/Wilson to LSU/FSU). Collin takes OVER 6.5 (+110), makes it ~6.35 (his spread number 6.7); Stuckey projects 6.7 and it's his flyer too.

teams.qb_status: Battle — Tayven Jackson (Indiana) / Cam Fancher / Jacurri Brown
teams.key_avoids: Easy non-con (Jackson State, NC A&T, then UNC home) — likely 3-0 start. But road Big 12 slate (Kansas State, Cincinnati, Baylor, Texas Tech, BYU late) projects ~0-5. Seven winnable home games (Jackson State, NC A&T, UNC, Kansas, West Virginia, Houston, Oklahoma State) — many vs other resetting teams; a 6-1 home run is the ceiling.
teams.bboc_notes: COMPLETE RESET and a fade lean — 93rd in returning production (dead last in the Big 12), ~70 new players, could start 8-9 transfers on offense. Scott Frost returns as new HC; the big question both hosts pose is WHICH Scott Frost — the UCF 0-12-to-13-0 version or the Nebraska dumpster fire. New DC Alex Grinch is a red flag: 'things have gotten worse everywhere he's been.' Three-way QB battle — Collin and Stuckey agree that if Cam Fancher wins it, the under is automatic; Tayven Jackson (Indiana) is the preferred option. Lost RJ Harvey (a monster) and every WR; DL should still be good (Nigel Lee/Malachi Lawrence, 10 sacks) but the LB corps is entirely portal and the secondary is light on talent facing Big 12 rushing attacks. Stuckey projects ~5.3, leans under, no interest as a flyer; Collin's problem with the under is the easy 2-0 start. When you line up the opposing coaches, both hosts 'take the other coach.'

teams.key_avoids: Plays SIX of the top eight; AVOIDS Texas Tech and Baylor; gets Iowa State and Arizona State at home. Only 4 Big 12 home games, FIVE road (Houston, TCU, Utah, West Virginia, Kansas State) — Stuckey sees ~1-4 there. Collin hates the draw of elite secondaries (Houston, BYU, TCU, Iowa State, Utah). Georgia Tech week one (home dogs) is a big swing.
teams.key_injury: Deion Sanders' health/availability an open question all season — hosts unsure his medical issues are fully cleaned up; where is the team if he isn't there.
teams.bboc_notes: Massive reset — lost Shedeur Sanders and four WRs (incl. Travis Hunter, also gone on D) to the NFL; last year's identity WAS the passing game (5,200 yds, 27 TD, 3 INT while the team ran 2.5 YPC and gave up 43 sacks). It flips to run-heavy with Kaidon Salter (dual-threat, 56 pass/21 rush TD career, careful with the ball) and freshman JuJu Lewis in packages. The RBs terrify both hosts — Hayden + Welch forced 15 missed tackles on 108 carries ('you can force a missed tackle by tying your shoes'). Right side of the OL a big question. The D is the strength: Robert Livingston (13th havoc, 15th pass-success, 20th finishing drives) despite losing six of top eight tacklers; needs a second corner and the JUCO LBs (Hughes/French) to hit. Last year they were +12 in turnovers and played a schedule full of disaster teams. HOST SPLIT: Stuckey thinks the market got too low (projects 5.7, won't go under 5.5); Collin bets UNDER 3.5 Big 12 wins on the brutal secondary-heavy slate.

teams.qb_status: Battle — Hauss Hejny (TCU) / Zane Flores (both young, never started)
teams.key_avoids: BRUTAL finish for a resetting team: at Texas Tech, at Kansas, Kansas State, at UCF, Iowa State. 5 Big 12 home games; road games Oklahoma State draws UCF, Kansas, Arizona, Texas Tech. Likely 2-1 start (beat UT Martin, Tulsa; lose to Oregon).
teams.bboc_notes: COMPLETE RESET after a 3-9 collapse and a hard fade — the OL lost eight players (264 combined starts) and now has THREE OL coaches; could start nine transfers on defense, and both hosts pan the incoming OL (all bad at lower-level prior stops). New OC Doug Meacham (Air Raid, back from the 2005-12 era) means a heavy-passing plan, but do they have the QB (young Hauss Hejny/Zane Flores), WRs (nine career starts), or OL to run it? New DC Todd Grantham imports a 3-4 — Collin's central objection: Gundy has rewired blocking schemes mid-season for years AND is now rewiring defensive personnel/scheme with players never recruited for a 3-4 ('firebomb Hail Marys'). Gundy's 18-year bowl streak snapped; sizable dog to reach a bowl (over 5.5 at +160). Stuckey projects 4.6, no interest either way. Collin is in the 3s, projects 2.8 total wins, going hard UNDER regardless of number.

teams.qb_status: Battle — McCay Hillstead / Bear Bachmeier (Stanford) / Borg
teams.key_avoids: Easy non-con but only 4 Big 12 home games (one is Utah, out for revenge). Road games Colorado, Arizona, Iowa State, Texas Tech, Cincinnati. The only passing offenses that scare the depleted secondary — Texas Tech and TCU — both come late, after a bye. Terrible spot: Holy War then at Iowa State ('nobody wants to be in Ames' after that).
teams.key_injury: OL injuries in spring (Gentry, from Michigan); WR room hurt (lost Lassiter to NFL, Marian to Miami).
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts land on 6.6 and pass — no QB to win the league. Jake Retzlaff left in an off-season scandal; neither host liked him (12-18 BTT/TOWP, boom-or-bust, but he was also the #2 rusher with 500+ yds — Collin says that mattered more than his arm). The replacement battle (McCay Hillstead, Stanford transfer Bear Bachmeier the highest-upside but very young, Borg) has only six career starts. The under is taking money as the number fell from 8.5 to 7.5 to 6.5. The real story was Jay Hill's defense (Y2) — the #1 pass D last year (13 TD allowed, 22 INT, most in FBS), but it loses its entire DL, LB Taggart, and secondary pieces; Collin is worried the new edges (235/255 lbs) are too light to hold up. Coaching continuity elsewhere (Sitake Y10, OC Roderick Y5). Regression flags after winning their close games. Stuckey doesn't think they have the QB play to win the conference; out of the flyer conversation.

teams.key_avoids: AVOIDS Arizona State, Texas Tech, and Kansas State; hosts Baylor and Iowa State. 5 Big 12 home games, draws four of the bottom five. Best schedule structure in the conference — Collin couldn't find another team that faces NO opponent coming off a bye; byes fall before at-Kansas and vs Arizona. Every game 'winnable' (opens vs Nebraska, neutral, TD dog).
teams.key_injury: DT Dontay Corleone (nose, 'the clubhouse guy') back with a clean bill of health after a blood-clot issue — must stay healthy.
teams.bboc_notes: Collin is OVER 6.5 (+124), makes it 7.3; Stuckey projects 6.5 and leans over but neither trusts Dave Satterfield — they've bet Cincy on Saturdays but never long-term because the team blows leads and gets out-coached in second halves (125th in the 'middle eight'). Finally fired Kerry Coombs after special-teams disasters. Year two of the 3-3-5 (Iowa State clone) transition; DL should step up with Corleone, Coleman and Hunt back healthy — the key is generating a pass rush; secondary a concern but corner Matthew McDoom (Coastal, 10 PBU/3 INT) is a get. Offense lost its star RB and top-six WRs plus four OL (three to the NFL) — LT Cotton (South Dakota, 6'7"/315, pro prospect) must hit. QB Brendan Sorsby (18 TD/7 INT but 9 BTT/13 TOWP, bottom-ten in explosiveness) has to be more consistent and lost four of his top five targets. Much more experienced roster (bottom-20 to top-25). A sharp group loves them but the fourth-quarter mistakes keep costing covers.

teams.qb_status: Battle — Nicco Marchiol / Jaylen Henderson (Texas A&M) / Max Brown
teams.key_avoids: Only 4 Big 12 home games. Road slate (Kansas, BYU, UCF, Houston, Arizona State) is full of uncertainty teams — only Arizona State is clearly tough (2nd-to-last game). Tough home slate in Morgantown (good HFA); hosts Pitt (Backyard Brawl, huge). Tricky non-con opener at Ohio. HORRIBLE spot: Backyard Brawl then at Kansas (off a bye).
teams.bboc_notes: Complete reset — ~80th in returning production, 16 of 22 two-deep on each side are transfers. Rich Rodriguez returns as new HC (zone-read, tempo, RPO, top-5 pace) — the only long-shot (45-1) Stuckey would entertain. New DC Zach Alley (won a bidding war vs Oklahoma; ex-Jacksonville State/OU) is highly regarded. Three-way QB battle; both hosts think Jaylen Henderson (A&M, dual-threat) fits best. Skill talent exists (RBs, WR Singleton from Jacksonville State knows the system), but the interior OL is small (295-lb center on inside zone) and entirely transfer-reliant — the swing factor. Secondary was so bad last year it should improve by subtraction. HOST SPLIT/spot-play framing: Stuckey shows value in the OVER and calls it his flyer; Collin is at 4.9 (under 5.5) but wants to bet WVU OVERS in individual games (top-5 tempo + leaky D = shootouts) and specifically bet against them at Kansas on Sept 20. Neither is fading RichRod.

teams.key_avoids: Five home games in the first six — possible hot/heat-edge start (2-0 vs Hawaii, Weber). But only 4 Big 12 home games. The Kansas State game is NON-CONFERENCE (in Dublin, in the heat, no breaks, KSU on thought travel) — Collin loves it as a bet spot. Winnable: Oklahoma State, BYU, coin-flip Colorado, at Cincy. Kansas health in November a factor.
teams.key_injury: Projected starting LT health in question; more injuries piling up on an already-thin OL.
teams.bboc_notes: The segment was nearly cut — hosts realized at the wrap-up ('we forgot Arizona') and did a rushed '2-minute Arizona.' New OC Seth Doege (Marshall, Air Raid) and new DC Danny Gonzalez bring ANOTHER 3-3-5; a wave of transfer QBs (incl. a Purdue transfer) install an air-raid. Bullish case = tons of injuries last year (three defensive captains drafted). Bearish: lost their two best WRs incl. first-rounder Tetairoa McMillan, RB Conley and LT to the NFL; OL is a mess (a Hawaii center who's never played center), DL unimpressive, 55 new players with little proven talent. Stuckey expected to be higher/on an over but dug in and DOWNGRADED them (projects 5.2) — questions all over, would go over but isn't running to bet it. Collin prefers the OVER 5.5, wants to let 'influencer' under-money sink the line, and loves specific betting spots (esp. the neutral Kansas State game). Skeptical of HC Brent Brennan's staying power; not a Brennan believer after San Jose State stayed fine and Arizona 'went down the tubes.'
